200tdi.intro: is often considered one of the most dependable engines ever fitted to a Defender

repair.when: Every 60k miles or 5 years — non-negotiable maintenance
Piston-valve contact means little is left to repair
Catch it early — straightforward repair on a well-maintained unit
Specialist rebuild is routine; far cheaper than replacement

buy.text: Documented timing belt change within the last 60k miles or 5 years
No signs of overheating or coolant loss (head gasket health)
Clean cold start with minimal smoke
A pre-1994 example with the 200Tdi — the last of the truly mechanical Defender diesels

avoid.text: No timing belt history — assume it's overdue and budget £500–£800 immediately
Overheating history or a pressurised coolant system — head gasket may be failing
Hard starting or significant black smoke — injection pump may be worn
Excessive oil leaks around the rear of the engine — could indicate rear main seal or more serious issues

200tdi.verdict: The **200Tdi** is often considered one of the most dependable engines ever fitted to a Defender — a **2.5-litre mechanical turbo-diesel** with **no ECU** and global parts availability. Its reputation is built on simplicity and torque, not refinement. The rubber timing belt is its one real vulnerability — maintain that and the **200Tdi** will outlast the chassis around it.

300tdi.intro: is a proven, simple turbo-diesel and one of the most popular engines in classic Land Rovers

repair.when: Every 60k miles or 5 years — fit the uprated backplate
Valve damage usually makes a rebuild or replacement the only option
Worth repairing if the head isn't cracked

buy.text: Timing belt and backplate replaced within the last 60k miles or 5 years
Temperature stays steady when towing or in traffic
Starts cleanly hot and cold with little smoke
Service history showing regular oil and filter changes

avoid.text: No timing belt history — budget £650–£950 straight away
Signs of overheating or coolant loss — possible head or gasket damage
Diesel leaks around the injection pump
Heavy oil leaks or oil in the coolant

300tdi.verdict: The **300Tdi** is a robust, **fully mechanical 2.5-litre turbo-diesel** that is easy to work on and well supported with parts. Keep the **timing belt and backplate** on schedule and the cooling system healthy, and it will reward you with very long service life.

td5.intro: is a strong five-cylinder diesel with real character, but it rewards owners who know its weak points

repair.when: Fix early before oil reaches the ECU
Worth it if the bottom end is healthy
Preventative fix is cheap; a seized engine is not
Simple repair — fix it and move on
Crank and bearing damage means rebuild or replace

buy.text: Evidence the injector loom and seals have been replaced
Steady temperature and no unexplained coolant loss
Smooth idle with no misfire or limp mode
Oil pump bolt fix done by a specialist

avoid.text: Oil in the injector loom plug or ECU connector
Mayonnaise under the oil cap — possible cracked head
Knocking or low oil pressure warnings

td5.verdict: The **Td5** is a tough **2.5-litre five-cylinder diesel** with plenty of torque. Its known issues — the **injector loom, cylinder head and oil pump bolt** — are well understood and fixable. Buy one with evidence of that work and it can be very long-lived.

m47.intro: is a capable BMW-sourced diesel, provided the turbo and intake are looked after

repair.when: Replace before debris reaches the engine
Fix at the first cold-start rattle
Routine repair for hard cold starts
Usually rebuild or replace once knocking

buy.text: Regular oil changes with the correct specification
Smooth boost with no whistle or blue smoke
No rattle on a cold start

avoid.text: Whistling turbo or oil in the intercooler pipes
Cold-start rattle from the timing chain
Limp mode or boost fault codes

m47.verdict: The **M47 2.0 diesel** is a strong, economical unit. Look after the **turbo, intake and oil** and it is a dependable choice; neglect them and turbo or bearing failure become expensive quickly.

kseries.intro: is a light, lively petrol engine — but one that is very intolerant of overheating

repair.when: Fit an MLS gasket and steel dowels
Fix immediately to protect the head

buy.text: Head gasket already upgraded to MLS with steel dowels
Coolant clean and at the correct level

kseries.verdict: The **1.8 K-Series** is light and willing, but its **head gasket and cooling system** are its weak points. With an **upgraded gasket** and a healthy cooling system it is perfectly usable — buy on condition and history, never on price alone.

kv6.intro: is a smooth V6 petrol whose life depends almost entirely on its cooling system and timing belts

repair.when: Fix at the first sign of loss
Replace both belts and tensioners together
Worth it if the heads aren't warped

buy.text: Proof of timing belt replacement on schedule
Cooling pipes and expansion tank recently replaced

avoid.text: No timing belt history — budget £800–£1,200 immediately
Coolant loss or a sweet smell from the engine bay

kv6.verdict: The **2.5 V6** is smooth and refined, but it is **unforgiving of cooling-system neglect**. Buy one with **belt and cooling history** and it is a pleasant engine; without it, budget for that work before anything else.

aj41.intro: is a classic Rover V8 with a great sound, but liner and overheating issues need careful checking

repair.when: Worth it if liners are sound
When the block is beyond re-sleeving

buy.text: Evidence of top-hat liners or a recent rebuild
No coolant loss and no pressurised hoses when cold

avoid.text: Coolant loss or hoses that are hard when the engine is cold

aj41.verdict: The **4.0 Rover V8** delivers a great sound and smooth power, but **liner slip** is its real risk. Look for evidence of **top-hat liners** or a quality rebuild, and keep the cooling system perfect.

ajv6.intro: is a strong supercharged petrol V6 that is refined and quick, with a few well-known cooling and drive issues

repair.when: Fix early to protect the heads
At the first sign of rattle

buy.text: Full main dealer or specialist history
Water pump replaced or no coolant loss

ajv6.verdict: The **3.0 supercharged V6** is fast and refined. Its known issues — **cooling, supercharger isolator and timing chain** — are well understood. Buy with history and it is a strong engine.

tdv6.intro: is a smooth, torquey V6 diesel — but crankshaft failure makes history and condition critical

repair.when: Replace both belts at the interval
Worth it if the engine is healthy
Engine-out repair; rebuild often best value

buy.text: Timing and fuel pump belts replaced on schedule
No knocking from the bottom end
Smooth boost with no limp mode

avoid.text: Any knocking or low oil pressure warning
Gaps in service history or long oil-change intervals
Oil in the coolant or coolant in the oil

tdv6.verdict: The **3.0 TDV6/SDV6** is smooth and powerful, but **crankshaft failure** is its big risk. Buy only with **frequent oil changes** on record — and if the crank has gone, a **quality rebuild** is usually better value than a used engine.

tdv8.intro: is a hugely torquey V8 diesel, but repair costs reflect its complexity

repair.when: Worth it if the engine is sound

tdv8.verdict: The **4.4 TDV8/SDV8** offers enormous torque and refinement, but its **turbos, cooling and bottom end** are expensive to fix. Buy with full history and budget sensibly for maintenance.

duratorq.intro: is an economical Ford-derived diesel that is reliable if its DPF and timing belt are looked after

repair.when: Worth it if the engine is sound

buy.text: Mix of long and short journeys in its history

avoid.text: DPF warning light or limp mode

duratorq.verdict: The **2.2 Duratorq** is economical and generally reliable. Keep the **DPF and timing belt** in order and it is a sensible, low-cost engine to own.

ecoboost.intro: is a punchy turbocharged petrol engine with a handful of known cooling and turbo issues
ecoboost.verdict: The **2.0 EcoBoost** is quick and refined. Watch the **cooling system** closely and it is a capable engine — overheating is the one thing it does not forgive.

aj200d.intro: is an efficient modern Ingenium diesel, but its rear-mounted timing chain needs careful attention

repair.when: Fix at the first start-up rattle
Worth it if the engine is sound

buy.text: Oil changed on time with the correct low-SAPS spec
No rattle on a cold start
Any timing chain recall or update work completed

avoid.text: Oil level rising between services (fuel dilution)

aj200d.verdict: The **2.0 Ingenium diesel** is efficient and refined, but the **timing chain** is its weak point. Buy only with **on-time servicing** and investigate any rattle immediately — early action is far cheaper than a replacement engine.

aj200p.intro: is a strong, modern Ingenium petrol engine with a timing chain that needs watching

buy.text: Full service history with the correct oil

aj200p.verdict: The **2.0 Ingenium petrol** is punchy and smooth. Keep on top of **servicing and the timing chain** and it is a good engine — most expensive failures start as ignored warning signs.

i3phev.intro: pairs a small turbo petrol with hybrid power, so diagnosis matters more than ever

repair.when: Worth it if the engine is sound

i3phev.verdict: The **1.5 PHEV** is efficient, but hybrid faults can mimic engine problems. Always get a **full diagnostic** before agreeing to engine work.

aj300d.intro: is a powerful, refined six-cylinder Ingenium diesel with mild-hybrid assistance

repair.when: Worth it if the engine is sound

aj300d.verdict: The **3.0 Ingenium six-cylinder diesel** is smooth and powerful. Its risks are **DPF-related oil dilution and timing chain wear** — buy with history and act early on warning signs.

aj300p.intro: is a smooth, powerful six-cylinder Ingenium petrol with mild-hybrid or plug-in assistance
aj300p.verdict: The **3.0 Ingenium six-cylinder petrol** is refined and quick. Most issues are **hybrid-system or cooling related** and fixable — get a full diagnostic before assuming the worst.

aj133.intro: is the legendary 5.0 supercharged V8 — thrilling, but expensive when neglected

repair.when: Fit updated parts at the first rattle

buy.text: Full history with timing chain update completed

aj133.verdict: The **5.0 supercharged V8** is magnificent, but its **timing chain and water pump** need attention. Buy one with these updates done and it is a deeply rewarding engine.

n63.intro: is a powerful BMW-sourced twin-turbo V8 that rewards meticulous maintenance

buy.text: No coolant or oil leaks in the hot-vee

n63.verdict: The **4.4 twin-turbo V8** is hugely powerful, but **oil consumption and hot-vee heat** are its weak spots. Buy with **meticulous history** and budget accordingly.

s68.intro: is the newest BMW-sourced twin-turbo V8 — still young, so prevention matters most

buy.text: No leaks or excessive oil consumption

s68.verdict: The **4.4 S68 twin-turbo V8** is still a young engine with **few proven failure patterns**. Prioritise **main dealer history** and remaining warranty, and keep servicing ahead of schedule.
